text:
maya: quick check — i'm updating a terraform module that manages the batch service account + IRSA role. terraform plan shows the SA will be replaced because the eks annotation key is changing. is there a safe rollout path?

ev an: which exact annotation change? can you paste the plan diff? :eyes:

maya: plan snippet: 
```
# kubernetes_service_account.batch will be replaced
-/+ resource "kubernetes_service_account" "batch" {
  - metadata {
      - annotations = {
          - "eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn" = "arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/old-batch-role"
        }
    }
  + metadata {
      + annotations = {
          + "eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn" = aws_iam_role.batch.arn
        }
    }
}
```

maya: provider is kubernetes v2.12.0 — i think upstream plan says replacement because the annotation value references an aws resource?

ev an: terraform's kubernetes provider will sometimes do a replace when there are computed fields in annotations. but usually annotations are mutable. two practical options: patch the SA in-cluster first, or tell tf to ignore_changes on that annotation then apply the role change.

ash: +1 to ignore_changes for a short window. example: 
```hcl
resource "kubernetes_service_account" "batch" {
  metadata {
    name = "batch-worker"
    namespace = var.namespace
    annotations = {
      "eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn" = aws_iam_role.batch.arn
    }
  }

  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = [metadata[0].annotations]
  }
}
```

jamie: careful: ignoring all annotations could hide real changes. instead target the exact key: `ignore_changes = [metadata[0].annotations["eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn"]]` — but terraform can't reference map key in ignore_changes in older versions. if that's not supported, do a targeted patch.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: FYI — if you patch SA annotation, workload pods using projected tokens should pick up the role after restart (service account token is mounted per-pod at creation).

maya: thinking flow: 1) create aws_iam_role for new ARN (already done), 2) kubectl patch sa batch-worker -n infra --patch '{"metadata": {"annotations": {"eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn":"arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/new-batch-role"}}}' 3) restart daemonset/dep to pick up token 4) run terraform apply but with `-target=aws_iam_role.batch` removed so tf doesn't try to replace SA. any issues?

ev an: that works. small caveat: IRSA relies on the cluster's OIDC provider being present and the role's trust relationship matching the SA subject (system:serviceaccount:namespace:name). verify trust policy.

ash: also verify projected token TTLs for long-running jobs — if you're rotating credentials, make sure token requests use `aud` and `expirationSeconds` appropriately. example pod spec fragment: 
```yaml
volumeMounts:
- name: sa-token
  mountPath: /var/run/secrets/tokens
volumes:
- name: sa-token
  projected:
    sources:
    - serviceAccountToken:
        audience: sts.amazonaws.com
        expirationSeconds: 86400
        path: token
```

maya: nice. one more: terraform state currently shows kubernetes_service_account.batch exists. if i patch in-cluster first, do i need to import anything?

jamie: no import needed if tf already tracks the SA. Just update in-cluster then run `terraform plan` — tf will usually detect drift and attempt to reapply unless you use ignore_changes or plan to accept the new value. if plan still forces replacement, you can `terraform apply -target=module.iam` then remove target and apply again after drift reconciled.

maya: ok i'll: 
- run `kubectl get sa batch-worker -n infra -o yaml` to confirm current annotations
- patch the annotation to new role ARN
- restart the deployments that use it (`kubectl rollout restart deploy/<name>`)
- run `terraform apply` with targeted approach or add short-lived ignore_changes

ash: sounds good. if you want me to watch, ping me when you patch so i can check OIDC logs.

maya: thanks — patching in ~10m and will update here. :thumbsup:
